# `Q-2-46` — Link reference definitions are not supported

> A line of the form `[ref]: https://example.com` is a link reference
> definition, which quarto-markdown does not collect. It renders as a
> visible paragraph.

## What this means

In Pandoc and CommonMark, a line like

```markdown
[gcc-toolset]: https://docs.redhat.com/...
```

is a *link reference definition*. It is consumed while parsing and
never appears in the output — its only job is to supply a URL to
`[label][gcc-toolset]` somewhere else in the document.

quarto-markdown does not collect these. The line is parsed as ordinary
paragraph text: a span, a colon, and a URL. So it renders, visibly, at
whatever point in the document it appears — usually as a stray block of
URLs at the bottom of the page:

```html
<p><span>gcc-toolset</span>: https://docs.redhat.com/...
<span>noexec</span>: https://man7.org/...</p>
```

## Why this happens

Reference-style links are a readability convention — they keep long
URLs out of the prose and collect them at the end of the file. A
document written that way for Pandoc carries its definition block along
when it is moved to quarto-markdown.

Note that a definition is only a definition at the **start of a line**.
A colon after a span mid-sentence — `text [label]: more` — is ordinary
prose and does not produce this warning.

## How to fix

Move each URL into an inline link at its use site, then delete the
definition line:

```markdown
See [the RedHat documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/...).
```

If a definition has no remaining uses, delete it outright. Quarto 1
consumed unused definitions and rendered nothing, so removing them is
what restores the output you expect.

`qmd-syntax-helper` does all of this:

```bash
qmd-syntax-helper check   -r reference-links "docs/**/*.qmd"
qmd-syntax-helper convert -r reference-links --in-place "docs/**/*.qmd"
```
